newsitem.title: GERMANY: German sugar industry maintains output forecast.
newsitem.headline: German sugar industry maintains output forecast.

text.p: The German sugar association WVZ sees no reason to adjust an August 26 sugar output forecast for 1996/97 of 3.868 million tonnes, up 1.9 percent from 1995/96, a spokesman for the industry body said.
"We characterise the beet crop as average...volume and yields will be slightly higher than last year," he said.
"Beet leaves are healthy and leaf weight is high, which points to reasonable sugar contents, although it is uncertain at what stage they will be reached given the rain pattern."
Harvesting, which in some parts of the country will start next week, could be disrupted by rain and cold weather.
Beet weights in the last WVZ test on September 2 had improved but still lagged last year by six percent, while the first test a month earlier had shown a 12 percent lag.
The crop benefited from rain in August after drought in the spring had depressed early results.
The fourth national fortnightly test is on Monday, September 14.

The area for the 1996/97 beet harvest will be up by 0.5 percent at 516,000 hectares, beet volumes should be steady at 26 million tonnes and sugar content could be higher at 17 percent (16.73 in 1995/96), WVZ said.
